summary.tldr: Directs the Health Minister to develop a national heart failure framework, with consultation, reporting and follow-up on its results.
what_it_does: Requires the Minister of Health to develop a national framework to improve heart failure prevention, diagnosis, management and evaluation.
Requires the framework to include early detection, patient and caregiver education, guideline-directed therapy, multidisciplinary care, and remote monitoring or virtual visits.
Requires the framework to address care gaps, especially in rural, remote and underserved communities.
Requires the framework to include patient outcome research, performance reporting, a national heart failure registry, and use of the Canadian Community Health Survey.
Requires the Minister to consult provincial governments, Indigenous governing bodies, health professionals, researchers, patients and caregivers, and to hold at least one conference within 12 months.
Requires the Minister to table the framework within 18 months, publish it online, and report within five years on its effectiveness and the current state of diagnosis and treatment.
summary.background: The bill says the framework is meant to improve access to heart failure prevention, diagnosis and treatment, and to reduce financial and operational burdens on the health system.
